title: Rearranging Real Energy Formulas
summary:
This capstone puts every earlier skill to work on the **actual formulas** you meet in thermodynamics and energy systems. Nothing new — just the same golden rule (do the same to both sides) and inverse operations from [[al01]], now applied where it counts. The point is to make these rearrangements feel routine, so the physics is the hard part, not the algebra.

**Energy balance — $Q = mc\,\Delta T$.** To find a specific heat or a temperature rise, isolate the wanted letter. For $c$: it's multiplied by $m$ and $\Delta T$, so divide by both, $c = \dfrac{Q}{m\,\Delta T}$. For the rise: $\Delta T = \dfrac{Q}{mc}$. Same pattern every time — divide by everything multiplying your target.

**Efficiency — $\eta = \dfrac{W}{Q}$.** A fraction, so the same denominator trick as density. For the work out, $W = \eta Q$; for the heat in, $Q = \dfrac{W}{\eta}$ (lift $Q$ from the denominator by multiplying, then divide by $\eta$).

**Carnot efficiency — $\eta = 1 - \dfrac{T_C}{T_H}$.** This trips people up because the variable is buried in a subtracted fraction. Peel it in order: move the 1 ($\dfrac{T_C}{T_H} = 1 - \eta$), then multiply by $T_H$: $$T_C = T_H(1 - \eta).$$ A clean example of 'undo the +/− before the ×/÷'.

**Ideal gas — $pV = nRT$.** Whatever you want, divide by the product of the other three. $T = \dfrac{pV}{nR}$, $n = \dfrac{pV}{RT}$, $V = \dfrac{nRT}{p}$ — all the same one-step move.

**Kinetic energy — $KE = \tfrac12 mv^2$** (a squared variable). Undo the $\tfrac12$ and $m$ first, then the square last: $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2\,KE}{m}}$ — square-root applied to the *whole* right-hand side.

**Exergy of heat — $X = \left(1 - \dfrac{T_0}{T}\right)Q$.** Combines a bracket and a fraction, but it's still layers: divide by $Q$, then handle the bracket as in the Carnot case. The habit to carry away: **identify the target, list what's wrapped around it, and unwrap in reverse order — applying every step to both whole sides.** Do that and any energy formula bends to your needs.

equations.name: Energy balance Q = m c ΔT
equations.useWhen: Heating/cooling problems. Divide by everything multiplying the letter you want — $c$, $m$ and $\Delta T$ are all just factors.
equations.note: Use absolute or relative temperatures consistently; $\Delta T$ is the same in K or °C.

equations.name: Efficiency η = W / Q
equations.useWhen: Any input/output efficiency. For $Q$ (in the denominator), multiply both sides by $Q$ first, then divide by $\eta$.
equations.note: $\eta$ is dimensionless (0–1). The same shape as COP, capacity factor and value factor.

equations.name: Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T_C/T_H
equations.useWhen: Finding a reservoir temperature from an efficiency. Undo the '$1-$' first (move it across), then deal with the fraction.
equations.note: Temperatures must be **absolute (K)**. A buried subtracted fraction — peel the +/− before the ×/÷.

equations.name: Ideal gas & kinetic energy
equations.useWhen: Gas-law rearrangements (divide by the product of the others) and any squared-variable formula (strip the factors, then square-root last).
equations.note: For $v$: multiply by 2, divide by $m$, then take the root of the *whole* side. Keep the positive root.

glossary.definition: Energy to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1 K, in $Q = mc\,\Delta T$. Rearranged: $c = Q/(m\,\Delta T)$.
Useful work out ÷ heat in, $\eta = W/Q$. Dimensionless, between 0 and 1; rearranges like any fraction.
The ceiling efficiency between two reservoirs, $\eta = 1 - T_C/T_H$ (temperatures in kelvin). Rearranges to $T_C = T_H(1-\eta)$.
Heat moved ÷ work in for a heat pump/fridge. A Carnot heat pump has $COP = T_H/(T_H - T_C)$ — another fraction to rearrange.
$pV = nRT$. Any one variable is found by dividing by the product of the others; $R$ is the gas constant.
$KE = \tfrac12 mv^2$. To get speed, isolate $v^2$ then square-root: $v = \sqrt{2\,KE/m}$.
Work potential of heat from a reservoir at $T$: $X = (1 - T_0/T)Q$. A bracket-and-fraction rearrangement combining earlier scenarios.
Temperature in kelvin (K). Efficiency, gas-law and exergy formulas require it — a frequent source of errors if °C is used by mistake.

tips: **Same recipe every time:** identify the target letter, list what's wrapped around it, unwrap in reverse order, apply each step to both whole sides, then check with numbers.
**Fractions: lift the denominator first.** For $\eta = W/Q$, get $Q$ by multiplying both sides by $Q$ before dividing by $\eta$ — exactly like density in [[al01]].
**Subtracted fractions (Carnot, exergy): undo the '1−' first.** Move the constant across, *then* clear the fraction. $\eta = 1 - T_C/T_H \Rightarrow T_C = T_H(1-\eta)$.
**Squared variable ⇒ root it last.** In $KE = \tfrac12 mv^2$, remove $\tfrac12$ and $m$, then square-root the whole other side to get $v$.
**Use kelvin in efficiency, gas-law and exergy formulas.** Rearranging is pointless if the temperature units are wrong — convert °C to K first.
**Rearrange symbolically before plugging in numbers.** You get a reusable formula, fewer rounding errors, and a clear check of your algebra.
